shifts.summary: The exam was overall easy to moderate with most candidates attempting 77 to 89 questions well. Reasoning was generally easy, while quantitative aptitude leaned moderate. General awareness was easy for many, and English was easy overall. Time management and the new sectional timer were common concerns.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Candidates reported many statement‑based and matrix questions, with no clock or mirror types. Reasoning was generally easy, some found it very easy.

sections.name: General Awareness

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant was moderate overall, with many circle and trigonometry questions; time management was noted as a concern.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English was easy for most candidates, with grammar and active‑passive questions common; passages were moderate in length.

observations: Candidates noted time management was a challenge, especially in math and reasoning sections.
The paper pattern remained similar to previous years with no major changes.

Overall attempts were high, with many reporting 85‑89 well‑attempted questions.
disagreements: Overall difficulty was split between Easy to Moderate (3 reports) and Moderate (3 reports).
Quant difficulty was reported as Easy by three sources and Moderate by six sources.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 7 October 2026 was reported to have an overall difficulty ranging from easy to moderate, with some variation across the three shifts. Unofficial figures suggest that candidates attempted between 75 % and 89 % of the questions correctly, depending on the shift. SSC normalises scores across shifts to ensure a fair comparison of candidates. The analysis for shift 3 is still pending and will be added once the full data is available.

faqs.q: What was the overall difficulty level of the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 7 October 2026?
faqs.a: Across the reported shifts, the exam was described as easy to moderate overall. Shift 1 and shift 2 were both characterised as easy‑to‑moderate, while shift 3 was reported as moderate.

faqs.q: How many questions were candidates able to attempt correctly on average in the 7 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 exam?
faqs.a: Unofficial data shows good attempt rates of 77‑89 % for shift 1, 79‑84.2 % for shift 2, and 75‑82 % for shift 3.

faqs.q: Which sections were reported as easy or moderate in the 7 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 exam?
faqs.a: Reasoning and English were generally rated easy to moderate across all shifts. General Awareness was easy in shifts 1 and 2 but moderate to tough in shift 3. Quantitative Aptitude varied from easy to moderate in shift 1, easy to hard in shift 2, and moderate to tough in shift 3.

faqs.q: How does SSC normalise scores across the three shifts of the 7 October 2026 Tier 1 exam?
faqs.a: SSC applies a normalisation process that adjusts raw scores from each shift to a common scale, accounting for any differences in difficulty, so that all candidates are compared on an equal footing.

faqs.q: When will the analysis for shift 3 of the 7 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 exam be added?
faqs.a: The analysis for shift 3 is currently pending and will be posted after the shift’s full data becomes available.
